topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting histopathology observations to cellular changes and outlining the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Viral discovery of oncogenes and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular oncogenes and led to experimental assays for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of cancer mutations and illustrate their molecular mechanisms using the cell cycle and p53 as examples.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing how defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis drive genomic abnormalities.

topics.label: Multistep tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the stepwise accumulation of mutations during tumor development and how inherited cancer syndromes accelerate this pathway.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by reviewing the learning outcomes, suggesting supplementary reading, and previewing the next session.
